Methodology

Across every rating and clock, the Danish Gambit family scores 55.4% for White — we are 90% confident the real figure is between 55.3% and 55.4% — from 6.0M Lichess games across 9 variations. Win rate, draw rate and loss rate come from games played December 2023 to November 2025.

How the figures are made
Whose games these are
6.0M+ rated games played on Lichess (2023-12 to 2025-11). The games are Lichess’s and free for anyone to use. What is ours is the reading of them. Last rebuilt January 2026.
Which games we count
  • Rated games only — nothing casual.
  • Both players within 200 rating points of each other. A mismatch tells you about the gap, not about the opening.
  • At least 2 moves played.
  • A game is filed under White’s rating.
Why every number comes with a range
A number off a few hundred games is a guess. The same number off millions is a fact. The range is what tells them apart, and it is what the lists rank on — so an opening cannot reach the top on a lucky run of forty games. The more games behind a figure, the narrower its range.
How much we need before we say anything
An opening page needs 100 games. A gambit needs 50 games before we will say where it stops working. The chaos and trap lists need 500 games.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Danish Gambit win rate?

The Danish Gambit family scores 55.4% (range, 90% confident: 55.3% – 55.4%) for White, aggregated from 9 variations and 6.0M rated games from Lichess.

How many Danish Gambit variations are there?

9 Danish Gambit variations have a page of their own, each broken down by rating and by clock.

At what rating does the Danish Gambit perform best?

The Danish Gambit family performs best at 1600-1799, where it scores 55.9% for White (1.5M games). Performance may vary by specific variation.

Is the Danish Gambit better in blitz or rapid?

For White, UltraBullet (58.7%) outperforms Classical (54.1%) across all Danish Gambit variations.

How sharp is the Danish Gambit?

Danish Gambit games are 96.9% decisive (non-draws), with an average length of 31 moves. Sharpness varies by specific variation.

Is the Danish Gambit a good opening family?

The Danish Gambit family is good for White overall with a 53.8% (range, 90% confident: 53.7% – 53.8%) aggregated win rate. However, win rates vary significantly between the 9 variations—explore individual lines to find the best fit for your style.
